proposals.before: Zhao Hui, whose style was Chongguang, was a native of Cangzhou.
proposals.after: Zhao Hui, whose style was Chongguang, was a native of Chanzhou.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou (in the Puyang region), not Cangzhou (滄州); the place name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: When the Han founder journeyed to the Eastern Capital, his route passed through Shaan. Hui, in full armor, paid his respects by the roadside, took the reins of the imperial carriage, and escorted it to the temporary palace. The bond between sovereign and minister seemed renewed, and he was soon given the honorary rank of Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: When the Han founder journeyed to the Eastern Capital, his route passed through Shaan. Hui, in full armor, paid his respects by the roadside, took the reins of the imperial carriage, and escorted it to the temporary palace. The bond between sovereign and minister seemed renewed, and he was soon given the honorary rank of Grand Marshal.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 is acting/honorary Grand Marshal (太尉), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: When the Han founder traveled to the Eastern Capital, his route passed through Shaan; Hui, in military dress, paid court on the left of the road, took the reins of the imperial carriage and escorted it to the traveling palace; the bond between ruler and minister was as if newly sealed, and he was soon made acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: When the Han founder traveled to the Eastern Capital, his route passed through Shaan; Hui, in military dress, paid court on the left of the road, took the reins of the imperial carriage and escorted it to the traveling palace; the bond between ruler and minister was as if newly sealed, and he was soon made acting Grand Marshal.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 should be acting Grand Marshal, not Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: Li Shouzhen was in revolt at Pu, Zhao Sinian held Yong, and all three rebels supported one another. Shu forces were also brought through Dasan Pass, and the rebellion seemed unstoppable.
proposals.after: Li Shouzhen was in revolt at Pu, Zhao Siwan held Yong, and all three rebels supported one another. Shu forces were also brought through Dasan Pass, and the rebellion seemed unstoppable.
proposals.reason: 趙思綰 is Zhao Siwan (Siwan), not Zhao Sinian; 綰 is wǎn.

proposals.before: At the time Li Shouzhen rebelled at Pu, Zhao Sinian held Yong, and they all aided one another in turn with Jingchong; moreover Shu troops were brought out through Dasan Pass, and the momentum seemed unstoppable.
proposals.after: At the time Li Shouzhen rebelled at Pu, Zhao Siwan held Yong, and they all aided one another in turn with Jingchong; moreover Shu troops were brought out through Dasan Pass, and the momentum seemed unstoppable.
proposals.reason: 趙思綰 should be romanized Zhao Siwan, not Zhao Sinian.

proposals.before: Late in the Jin dynasty the Khitans held the Central Plains. The Han founder raised his standard at Jinyang and soon recovered the heartland, but Changshan alone remained in Khitan hands. Rao was then in that region. He joined Li Yun, Bai Zairong, and others in a sudden uprising and drove out the Khitan garrison entirely.
proposals.after: Late in the Jin dynasty the Khitans held the Central Plains. The Han founder raised his standard at Jinyang and soon recovered the heartland, but Changshan alone remained in Khitan hands. Rao was then in that region. He joined Li Jun, Bai Zairong, and others in a sudden uprising and drove out the Khitan garrison entirely.
proposals.reason: 李筠 is conventionally romanized Li Jun; Yun is a less standard reading of 筠 here.

proposals.before: At the end of Jin the Khitans held the Central Plains; the Han founder raised the banner of righteousness at Jinyang and soon recovered the various Xia lands; only Changshan commandery was held by the Khitans; at the time Rao was in that commandery; he then joined Li Yun, Bai Zairong, and their kind in seizing an opportune moment to rise in secret and drive out all their faction.
proposals.after: At the end of Jin the Khitans held the Central Plains; the Han founder raised the banner of righteousness at Jinyang and soon recovered the various Xia lands; only Changshan commandery was held by the Khitans; at the time Rao was in that commandery; he then joined Li Jun, Bai Zairong, and their kind in seizing an opportune moment to rise in secret and drive out all their faction.
proposals.reason: 李筠 should be Li Jun in standard historical romanization.

proposals.before: His original name was Fangjian. Early in the Guangshun reign, because it violated an imperial taboo, he changed it.
proposals.after: His original name was Fangjian (方簡). Early in the Guangshun reign, because it violated a temple taboo, he changed it.
proposals.reason: Clarify that the original given name is 方簡 (Fangjian), distinct from the later taboo-avoidance name 方諫.

decisions.after: At the end of the Later Jin, the Khitans held the Central Plains. The Later Han founder raised a righteous standard at Jinyang and soon recovered the central provinces, but Changshan Commandery remained under Khitan control. Rao was then in the commandery; he joined Li Yun, Bai Zairong, and the others in rising at an opportune moment and expelled the Khitan garrison.
decisions.reason: The historical 李筠 is conventionally Li Yun, so the proposed Li Jun is incorrect; the revision keeps the correct name and makes the dynastic references explicit.

decisions.after: His original name was Fangjian. Early in the Guangshun reign, he changed it because it violated a temple taboo.
